### PASTA AND RICE

Microwave cooking and conventional cooking of pasta, rice, and cereal require about the same amount of time, but the microwave is a more convenient method because you can cook and serve in the same dish. There is no stirring needed and leftover pasta tastes just like fresh cooked when reheated in the microwave oven.

#### Cooking Pasta and Rice: Tips and Techniques
- If you are planning to use rice or pasta in a casserole, undercook it so it is still firm.
- Allow for standing time with rice, but not for pasta
- The Pasta and Rice Cooking Tables below provide specific directions, with Power Level and cooking time settings for most common types of pasta and rice.

text:
## CARE AND CLEANING

For best performance and safety, keep the oven clean inside and outside. Take special care to keep the inner door panel and the oven front frame free of food or grease build-up. Never use rough powder or pads. Wipe the microwave oven inside and out, including the hood bottom cover, with a soft cloth and a warm (not hot) mild detergent solution. Then rinse and wipe dry. Use a chrome cleaner and polish on chrome, metal and aluminum surfaces. Wipe spatters immediately with a wet paper towel, especially after cooking chicken or bacon. Clean your oven weekly or more often, if needed.

### METAL RACK

Wash the metal rack with a mild soap and a soft or nylon scrubbrush. Dry completely. Do not use abrasive scrubbers or cleaners to clean rack.

### CLEANING THE GREASE FILTER

The grease filter should be removed and cleaned often, at least once a month.

1. To remove grease filter, slide filter to the side. Pull filter downward and push to the other side. The filter will drop out.

2. Wash in dishwasher or soak grease filter in hot water and a mild detergent. Rinse well and shake to dry. Do not use ammonia or place in a dishwasher. The aluminum filter will darken.
<PIC:Manual24_47>
{{image description: Underside line drawing of an over-the-range microwave with an arrow pointing to the bottom filter or vent area.}}


3. To reinstall the filter, slide it into the side slot, then push up and toward oven center to lock
<PIC:Manual24_48>
{{image description: Line drawing of hands washing a mesh grease filter under running water at a sink.}}


<PIC:Manual24_49>
{{image description: Underside drawing of the microwave with a bold arrow indicating the bottom filter or vent panel being pulled or slid out.}}

**CAUTION:**

To avoid risk of personal injury or property damage, do not operate oven hood without filter in place.

### CHARCOAL FILTER REPLACEMENT

If your oven is vented inside, the charcoal filter should be replaced every 6 to 12 months, and more often if necessary. The charcoal filter cannot be cleaned.

1. Unplug the oven or turn off power at the main power supply.
2. Remove the two vent grill mounting screws. (2 middle screws)

3. Tip the grill forward, then lift it out.
4. Remove old filter.
<PIC:Manual24_50>
{{image description: Installation/removal drawing of a microwave being held from both sides under a cabinet, with two screws shown above the top mounting area.}}


5. Slide a new charcoal filter into place. The filter should rest at the angle shown.
<PIC:Manual24_51>
{{image description: Front view of a microwave with the grille or vent opened. A hand pulls a mesh filter or charcoal filter outward, indicated by a bold arrow.}}


6. Slide the bottom of the grill into place. Push the top until it snaps into place. Replace the mounting screws. Turn the power back on at the main power supply and set the clock.
<PIC:Manual24_52>
{{image description: Front microwave view showing a large rectangular mesh filter installed behind the top grille above the door.}}


### COOKTOP/NIGHT LIGHT REPLACEMENT

1. Unplug the oven or turn off power at the main power supply.

2. Remove the bulb cover and mounting screws.
3. Replace bulb(s) with 30 or 40 watt appliance bulb(s)
4. Replace bulb cover and mounting screws.
5. Turn the power back on at the main power supply or plug in the oven.
<PIC:Manual24_53>
{{image description: Underside close-up of the microwave showing the bottom light covers, central vent/filter area, and a small screw or latch in the middle.}}


**CAUTION:**

To avoid personal injury or property damage, wear gloves when replacing light bulb

### OVEN LIGHT REPLACEMENT

1. Unplug oven or turn off power at the main power supply.
2. Remove the vent cover mounting screws. (2 middle screws)
3. Tip the cover forward, then lift out to remove.
4. Remove bulb holder
<PIC:Manual24_54>
{{image description: Drawing of a microwave being supported from both sides under a cabinet, with two top mounting screws shown above.}}

5. Lift up the bulb holder
<PIC:Manual24_55>
{{image description: Front top grille area of the microwave with a bold arrow pointing to a small rectangular light or filter housing behind the grille.}}

6. Replace bulb with a 30 or 40 watt appliance bulb.
7. Replace the bulb holder.
8. Slide the bottom of the vent cover into place. Push the top until it snaps into place. Replace the mounting screws. Turn the power back on at the main power supply or plug in the oven.
<PIC:Manual24_56>
{{image description: Front view with the microwave grille removed or opened, showing a rectangular filter or panel being pulled out toward the viewer.}}

1. Unplug oven or turn off power at the main power supply.
2. Remove the vent cover mounting screws. (2 middle screws)
3. Tip the cover forward, then lift out to remove.
4. Remove bulb holder
<PIC:Manual24_54>

7. Replace the bulb holder.
8. Slide the bottom of the vent cover into place. Push the top until it snaps into place. Replace the mounting screws. Turn the power back on at the main power supply or plug in the oven.
<PIC:Manual24_56>

pic_descriptions.description: Photo inside a microwave oven showing a glass dish of cooked vegetables or casserole on the turntable.
Warning symbol for electrical shock hazard, with a warning bar, exclamation triangle, hand, cord, and lightning bolt.
Grounding illustration showing a three-prong plug aligned with a grounded wall outlet.

Labeled front diagram of an over-the-range microwave. Callouts identify the door handle, window with metal shield, door safety lock system, model and serial number plate, metal rack, cooking guide, vent grill, oven control panel, grease filter, glass turntable, and cooktop or countertop light.

Oven specifications table: power supply 120 VAC, 60 Hz; input power 1,500 W; cooking power 1,000 W, IEC 60705 standard; frequency 2,450 MHz; rated current 13 A; outer dimensions 29 15/16 in x 16 7/16 in x 15 5/8 in; cavity volume 1.8 cu. ft.; net weight 60 lbs.

Microwave control panel diagram with numbered callouts. It shows a display, food keys such as Popcorn, Potato, Pizza, Cook, Reheat, Vegetable, Frozen Entree, Easy Cook, Auto Defrost, Time Defrost, and Quick Defrost, numeric keypad, Kitchen Timer, Clock, Light Timer, Help, Stop/Clear, Control Set-Up, Start, Power Level, Program, Hold Warm, Vent Hi/Low/Off, and Light Hi/Low/Off buttons.

Procedure and display table for Help. Step 1 says touch Help pad with display text TOUCH THIS KEYPAD THEN THE DESIRED FEATURE. Step 2 says touch Popcorn pad with display text explaining that the keypad pops microwave popcorn and sensing will remain until cooking time is calculated.
Procedure and display table for setting the clock. Steps show touching Clock, entering 8 0 0, and touching Start. Display examples read AM ENTER TIME OF DAY, 8:00 TOUCH START, and 8:00.

Procedure and display table for Kitchen Timer. Steps show touching Kitchen Timer, entering 3 0 0, and touching Start. Display examples read ENTER TIME IN MIN AND SEC, 3:00 TOUCH START, and timer and time counting down.

Control set-up table with columns No., Function, No., and Result. Functions include sound on/off control, clock on/off control, scroll speed control with slow, normal, and fast speed, and LBS/KG choice control with Lbs. or Kg.

Procedure and display table for changing defrost weight mode from Lbs to Kg. Steps show touching Control Set-Up, touching number 4, then number 2. Displays show SOUND ON/OFF TOUCH 1, CLOCK ON/OFF TOUCH 2, SCROLL SPEED TOUCH 3, LBS/KG CHOICE TOUCH 4; then LBS TOUCH 1 KG TOUCH 2; final display KG.

Light Timer procedure table. Steps show touching Light Timer, entering 2:00 for light on, touching Light Timer again, entering 7:00 for light off, then touching Start. Display examples include AM ENTER LIGHT ON TIME, 2:00 TOUCH LIGHT TIMER, AM ENTER LIGHT OFF TIME, 7:00 TOUCH START, and Time of day.

Procedure and display table for canceling Light Timer. Step 1 says touch Light Timer pad with display AM ENTER LIGHT ON TIME OR TOUCH CLEAR TO RESET THE TIMER. Step 2 says touch Stop/Clear pad; display returns to Time of day.
Procedure and display table for Easy Cook. It says touch Easy Cook pad 4 times; display says time counting down and power 100.
Procedure and display table for Hold Warm. Steps show touching Hold Warm pad and Start pad. Displays read HOLD WARM TOUCH START and WARM.
Small table listing food type and recommended quantity for Hold Warm: Liquid 1-2 cups, Dry 5-10 ozs.

Procedure and display table for Favorite Recipe. Steps show touching Favorite Recipe, entering cook time with number keypad 2 0 0, and touching Start. Displays include 1:30 TOUCH START OR ENTER NEW TIME, 2:00 TOUCH START OR POWER, and time counting down.
Procedure and display table for Favorite Recipe. Steps show touching Favorite Recipe and touching Start. Display shows 2:00 TOUCH START OR POWER, then time counting down.
Procedure and display table for timed cooking. Steps show entering cook time 8 3 0 and touching Start. Displays read 8:30 TOUCH START OR POWER, then time counting down, power 100.

Procedure and display table for cooking at a selected power level. Steps show entering cook time 7:30, touching Power Level, entering power level 7, and touching Start. Displays include ENTER POWER LEVEL 1 TO 10, P-70 TOUCH START, and time counting down and power 70.

Two-stage cooking procedure table. Steps show entering 3:00, touching Program, entering second cook time 7:30, touching Power Level, entering power level 7, and touching Start. Displays include ENTER COOKING TIME, ENTER POWER LEVEL 1 TO 10, P-70 TOUCH START, and time counting down.

Microwave power level chart with columns Power Level, Microwave Output, and Use. It lists 10 High at 100 percent for boiling water and cooking tender foods; 9 at 90 percent; 8 at 80 percent; 7 at 70 percent; 6 at 60 percent; 5 at 50 percent; 4 at 40 percent; 3 at 30 percent; 2 at 20 percent; 1 at 10 percent; and 0 at 0 percent standing time.

Procedure and display table for sensor Cook. Steps show touching Cook, choosing Casserole with number 2, then touching number 9 for More. Displays show SELECT MENU 1 TO 3, CASSEROLE, SENSING, and MORE. A small table lists Cook Time Less 7, Normal 8, More 9.
Procedure and display table for Popcorn. Step 1 says touch Popcorn pad; display shows POPCORN, then an arrow to SENSING.

Procedure and display table for Pizza. Step 1 says touch Pizza pad; display shows PIZZA, then an arrow to SENSING. Notes say four beeps sound and END displays when reheat time is over, and recommended amount is 1-3 slices, about 5 ozs. each.
Procedure and display table for Potato. Step 1 says touch Potato pad; display shows POTATO, then an arrow to SENSING.

Procedure and display table for Vegetable. Steps show touching Vegetable, choosing food category by touching number 2 for Frozen Vegetable, then sensing. Displays list FRESH TOUCH 1, FROZEN TOUCH 2, CANNED TOUCH 3; then FROZEN VEGETABLE and SENSING.

Procedure and display table for sensor Cook with category Rice. Steps show touching Cook and choosing food category number 3. Displays show SELECT MENU 1 TO 3, RICE, and SENSING. A category table lists Frozen Entree 1, Casserole 2, Rice 3.
Quantity table for Cook categories: Frozen Entree 10-21 ozs., Casserole 1-4 cups, Rice 1/2-2 cups.
Category table for Reheat touch pad numbers: Casserole 1, Dinner Plate 2, Soup/Sauce 3.
Procedure and display table for sensor Reheat. Steps show touching Reheat and choosing Casserole with number 1. Displays show SELECT MENU 1 TO 3, CASSEROLE, and SENSING.
Quantity table for Reheat categories: Casserole 1-4 cups, Dinner Plate 1-2 servings, Soup/Sauce 1-4 cups.
Auto Defrost category table listing Meat touch pad 1, Poultry touch pad 2, and Fish touch pad 3.

Procedure and display table for Auto Defrost. Steps show touching Auto Defrost, choosing Meat with number 1, entering weight with 1 and 2, and touching Start. Displays include MEAT TOUCH 1 POULTRY TOUCH 2 FISH TOUCH 3, ENTER WEIGHT, 1.2 LBS TOUCH START, and time counting down and DEFROST.

Weight conversion chart with equivalent ounce weight and pounds. It maps 1.6 to .10, 3.2 to .20, 4.0 to .25 one-quarter pounds, 4.8 to .30, 6.4 to .40, 8.0 to .50 one-half pounds, 9.6 to .60, 11.2 to .70, 12.0 to .75 three-quarter pounds, 12.8 to .80, 14.4 to .90, and 16.0 to 1.00 one pound.

Auto Defrost chart for meat with columns Food, At Beep, and Special Instructions. Beef, lamb, and pork rows tell the user to remove thawed portions, turn over, separate and rearrange, cover warm areas with aluminum foil, and place food on a microwavable roasting rack or baking dish. Some rows warn not to defrost less than 1/4 lb or less than 2 oz patties.

Auto Defrost chart for poultry. Chicken whole up to 6 lbs should be turned over, warm areas covered with aluminum foil, placed breast-side up on a microwavable roast rack, and finished in cold water. Cut-up chicken is separated and rearranged. Cornish hens and turkey breast under 6 lbs are turned over and finished with cold water.

Auto Defrost chart for fish and shellfish. Fish fillets are turned over and separated when partially thawed; steaks are separated and rearranged; whole fish is turned over and may be covered with foil. Shellfish rows for crabmeat, lobster tails, shrimp, and scallops say to break apart, turn over, or rearrange and place in a microwavable baking dish.

Procedure and display table for Time Defrost. Steps show touching Time Defrost, entering 2:00 with keypad 2 0 0, and touching Start. Displays read ENTER DEFROST TIME, 2:00 TOUCH START, and time counting down and DEFROST.
Procedure and display table for Quick Defrost. Step 1 says touch Quick Defrost pad with display GROUND BEEF 1.0 LBS TOUCH START. Step 2 says touch Start; display says time counting down and DEFROST.

Two-part installation diagram for a microwave rack inside the oven cavity. Each panel shows the rack on side supports and a magnified circular inset of the support hook area, with arrows pointing down to the detail.

Defrosting chart table with columns Food, Time, and Special Instructions. It lists meat, poultry, and fish/seafood items such as bacon, ground meat, roasts, chicken, Cornish hen, fillets, and shellfish, with times from about 2 to 18 minutes and instructions to turn food over, shield warm areas with foil, cover, and let stand.

Fish cooking chart with columns Fish, Power Level, Cooking Time, and Directions. Rows include fish fillets, fish steaks, whole fish, scallops, and shelled shrimp, with power levels HI or 7 and cooking times such as 3 1/2 to 6 minutes; directions mention arranging in a single layer, covering with vented plastic wrap, and letting stand.

Meat cooking chart with columns Meat, Power Level, Cooking Time, and Directions. It includes beef hamburgers, sirloin tip roast, lamb roast, bacon slices, pork chops, loin roast, and sausage links, with power levels HI, 5, or 3 and temperatures such as 135 degrees F, 145 degrees F, 155 degrees F, 165 degrees F, and 170 degrees F.

Poultry cooking chart with columns Poultry, Power Level, Cooking Time, and Directions. Rows include chicken pieces, whole chicken, and whole Cornish hens at power level HI, with minutes per pound and instructions to wash, place in a dish or rack, cover with waxed paper, turn or shield parts, and let stand covered with foil.

Pasta cooking chart with columns Pasta, Power Level, Cooking Time, and Directions. Rows include spaghetti, macaroni, lasagna noodles, and egg noodles, with water amounts, power levels HI and 5, cooking times, and directions to combine water and salt, cover or vent, stir, and drain.

Rice cooking chart with columns Rice, Power Level, Cooking Time, and Directions. Rows include long grain, brown, long grain and wild rice mix, and quick cooking rice, with water amounts, power levels HI and 5, cooking times, and directions to combine hot water and salt, stir, cover, and let stand.
Underside line drawing of an over-the-range microwave with an arrow pointing to the bottom filter or vent area.
Line drawing of hands washing a mesh grease filter under running water at a sink.
Underside drawing of the microwave with a bold arrow indicating the bottom filter or vent panel being pulled or slid out.
Installation/removal drawing of a microwave being held from both sides under a cabinet, with two screws shown above the top mounting area.
Front view of a microwave with the grille or vent opened. A hand pulls a mesh filter or charcoal filter outward, indicated by a bold arrow.
Front microwave view showing a large rectangular mesh filter installed behind the top grille above the door.
Underside close-up of the microwave showing the bottom light covers, central vent/filter area, and a small screw or latch in the middle.
Drawing of a microwave being supported from both sides under a cabinet, with two top mounting screws shown above.
Front top grille area of the microwave with a bold arrow pointing to a small rectangular light or filter housing behind the grille.
Front view with the microwave grille removed or opened, showing a rectangular filter or panel being pulled out toward the viewer.

Troubleshooting table with columns Problem and Possible Causes. Visible problem rows include oven not operating, interior light not working, oven not cooking, food cooking unevenly, undercooked or overcooked food, arcing sparks, display counting down but oven not cooking, and vent fan starting automatically.

Warning box with a triangular caution icon and the heading WARNING. The text warns that to avoid electrical shock causing personal injury or death, the outer case should not be removed and only an authorized servicer should remove it.

Question and answer table for microwave use. Questions include using a rack or two rack positions, using metal pans, why the fan runs, why the dish becomes hot, standing time, popcorn, best results, and steam from the air exhaust vent.
